title: Tell them the story of the town.
subtitle: A parable set before the people of Makkah
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to set an example before his people who denied him. Ibn Ishaq relayed reports that the town was Antioch, but {idea}some scholars were not sure of that.{/idea} The point is the pattern: {trap}messengers came, and the town had to choose.{/trap}
now: You hear a story in a talk and immediately think of someone else who needs it. {idea}The Quran tells stories so you will see yourself in them.{/idea} Read this one as if it is about your street.
old: Quran stories are about people long ago.
new: Each story is a mirror held up to me and my choices today.
try: As you read the next few verses, ask at each step: which person am I here?

title: Two were denied, so a third was sent.
subtitle: Allah reinforced His messengers
then: Ibn Kathir says the town {trap}hastened to disbelieve in the two{/trap}, so Allah {reward}supported and strengthened them with a third.{/reward} Together they said they were sent from the Lord who created them, calling to worship Him alone.
now: You tried to start a study circle with a friend and nobody came. {idea}Rejection was not the end of the messengers' work.{/idea} {reward}Sometimes Allah sends a third person just when you need one.{/reward}
old: If my good effort is rejected, it was a mistake to try.
new: Allah supports those who keep calling to good. Help can arrive after rejection.
try: Message one friend today and invite them to join you in one good deed.

title: You are only human like us.
subtitle: The oldest excuse for rejecting messengers
then: Ibn Kathir says they reasoned: {trap}we are human and you are human, so why would you get revelation and not us?{/trap} Many nations said the same, he notes, citing verses where people asked {trap}shall mere men guide us?{/trap}
now: Your cousin gives you good advice, and your first thought is: who is he to tell me, he messes up too. {trap}Dismissing the message because of the messenger is an old trick.{/trap} {idea}Weigh the words, not just the person.{/idea}
old: I only take advice from people who are better than me.
new: Truth can come through ordinary people. I should judge the message, not dismiss the messenger.
try: Think of one piece of good advice you rejected because of who said it. Try it today.

title: Our Lord knows we were sent to you.
subtitle: When you cannot prove it, Allah is your witness
then: Ibn Kathir explains their reply: {idea}Allah knows we are His messengers.{/idea} If they were lying, He would have taken vengeance on them, but {reward}He would make them prevail{/reward}, and everyone would learn whose end was good.
now: Someone at work accuses you of something you did not do, and you cannot prove it. {idea}You can still say: Allah knows.{/idea} {reward}That is not weakness. It is the strongest witness there is.{/reward}
old: If I cannot prove I am right, I have lost.
new: Allah knows the truth. His knowledge is enough for me.
try: If you feel misjudged today, say quietly: Allah knows, and leave it there.

title: Our only duty is to convey it clearly.
subtitle: The messengers knew the limits of their job
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}all we have to do is convey the message.{/idea} If you obey, {reward}happiness in this world and the next{/reward} is yours. If not, you will soon know the consequences.
now: You keep rewriting the message to your sibling, trying to get it perfect so they will finally listen. {idea}Be clear, be kind, then let it go.{/idea} The response is not your burden.
old: If they do not accept it, I explained it badly.
new: My duty is clear delivery. Acceptance is between them and Allah.
try: Say one clear, kind thing today that you have been holding back, then stop pushing.

title: You are bad luck for us.
subtitle: Blaming the reminder for the trouble
then: Qatadah said they claimed {trap}if something bad befalls us, it will be because of you.{/trap} Mujahid said they believed people like these messengers always brought punishment on a town. Then came {trap}the threat to stone them.{/trap}
now: Since that friend started reminding you to pray, you feel uncomfortable around them. {trap}You start avoiding them as if they bring bad vibes.{/trap} {idea}The discomfort may be your conscience waking up.{/idea}
old: Since that person came along, things feel worse. They must be the problem.
new: The reminder is not the bad luck. Sometimes discomfort is the start of change.
try: Thank, instead of avoid, the next person who reminds you of Allah.

title: Your bad omen is with you.
subtitle: Because you were reminded? No, you went too far
then: The messengers answered: {trap}your omens are thrown back at you.{/trap} Qatadah said it means, {idea}because we reminded you about Allah, you saw an evil omen in us{/idea}, but in truth they were a people who went beyond limits.
now: Every bad week you blame the boss, the traffic, the economy. {idea}The verse asks you to look at what you carry with you.{/idea} {reward}That is good news: it means you can change something.{/reward}
old: My problems are always caused by other people.
new: Some of my trouble travels with me. Owning it is the first step to fixing it.
try: Tonight, write one problem from today and one way you may have contributed to it.

title: A man came running from the far end of town.
subtitle: One ordinary believer stood up for the messengers

row.title: anyone
sub: even from the edge of town

then: Ibn Ishaq's reports say when the town resolved to kill the messengers, a man came running to help them. {idea}They said his name was Habib, a rope worker{/idea}, sickly, yet {reward}giving half his earnings in charity.{/reward}
now: Someone in the family group chat is being mocked for wearing hijab or for praying, and everyone stays silent. {idea}You are not the imam. You are not important.{/idea} {reward}You can still be the one who comes running.{/reward}
old: Speaking up is for people with status. I am nobody.
new: One ordinary person from the edge of town can stand up for the truth.
try: The next time someone is mocked for their faith, say one supportive sentence.

title: Follow those who ask you for nothing.
subtitle: Two signs of a trustworthy guide
then: The man gave his people two simple reasons. Ibn Kathir says the messengers {reward}asked no wages for the message{/reward} and {idea}were rightly guided in calling to the worship of Allah alone.{/idea}
now: Your feed is full of people who want something from you: a subscription, a click, a donation link. {idea}Notice who gives you good and asks nothing back.{/idea} That is a sign worth trusting.
old: The most popular voice is the one worth following.
new: A guide who wants nothing from me and points to Allah is worth listening to.
try: Unfollow one account today that only sells, and follow one that teaches for free.

title: Why should I not worship the One who made me?
subtitle: The simplest reason for faith
then: The man turns it into a personal question. Ibn Kathir paraphrases it: {idea}what is there to stop me from sincerely worshipping the One who created me?{/idea} He then reminds them that {trap}they too will return to Him for judgment.{/trap}
now: You find yourself needing a reason to pray today. {idea}Flip it around: why not?{/idea} The One who made your eyes, your hands, this morning, is asking for a few minutes.
old: I need a good reason to worship before I commit.
new: He made me. The real question is what is stopping me.
try: Before your next prayer, ask yourself this verse's question and answer it honestly.

title: If harm is meant for me, they could not save me.
subtitle: The helplessness of false gods
then: The man asks: {trap}shall I take other gods besides Him?{/trap} Ibn Kathir calls it a rebuke. These idols {trap}could neither harm nor benefit{/trap}, and if Allah willed harm, {idea}none could remove it but He.{/idea}
now: Lab results pending, you rely on the best clinic, the right connections, the insurance plan. {idea}They are means, not saviors.{/idea} {reward}The One who can remove harm is the One to ask first.{/reward}
old: With the right contacts and backup plans, I am covered.
new: Only Allah can remove harm. Everything else is just a means He may use.
try: Before your next appointment or big decision, ask Allah first, then use the means.

title: Then I would be clearly lost.
subtitle: Calling his own alternative by its name
then: He does not say you are in error. He says {idea}I would be in plain error{/idea} if I took them as gods. Ibn Kathir explains it means {trap}if I were to take them as gods instead of Allah.{/trap} He speaks of himself to soften their hearts.
now: When you want to correct someone, it is easy to say: you are wrong. {idea}This man said: if I did that, I would be wrong.{/idea} {reward}That is how you invite without attacking.{/reward}
old: Calling out other people's mistakes is the way to help them.
new: Speaking about myself first lets the truth reach others without a fight.
try: In your next disagreement, use an I sentence instead of a you sentence.

title: I have believed in your Lord, so hear me.
subtitle: Declaring faith openly, whatever it costs
then: Ibn Jarir thought he was speaking to the messengers: {idea}bear witness that I have believed.{/idea} The reports say his people then turned on him and killed him. Qatadah said {reward}he kept praying, O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know.{/reward}
now: Someone hurts you because of your faith, maybe a cruel comment from a coworker. {trap}You want to hit back.{/trap} {reward}This man, as he was being killed, prayed for his own people to be guided.{/reward}
old: When people hurt me for my faith, I have the right to hate them.
new: I can hold to my faith openly and still wish guidance for those who hurt me.
try: Make dua today for guidance for someone who has been unkind to you.
